data.title: What JetBlue Airways Bears Spotted Before The Slide
data.description:
JetBlue Airways grabbed headlines in 2026 as Spirit Airlines shut down and new Fort Lauderdale routes, premium products, and loyalty tie ups reshaped its story. For JetBlue Airways shareholders, the loss from the start of the year was 22.9%, including dividends. If you had bought in on 1 January leaning on forecasts of 6.9% revenue growth, a 6.8% profit margin and a 5.4x future P/E, which of those specific assumptions most clearly missed what actually unfolded?

The Two JetBlue Airways Stories Investors Were Weighing

The shares cost US$4.55 at the start of the period, and JetBlue Airways came with two very different but credible stories attached.

The bullish narrative saw fair value at US$6.9, built on revenue growth of 6.9% a year and profit margins reaching 6.8% within a 3 year window.

The bearish view put fair value at US$3, assuming a lower 4.1% revenue growth rate and warning that rising regulatory and environmental costs could squeeze margins even if they reached 6.8%.

What The Results Put To The Test For JetBlue Airways

JetBlue Airways leaned hard into Fort Lauderdale expansion, premium cabins and loyalty tie ups that echoed the bullish story of richer revenue per seat. The Q3 2026 report told a different side. Revenue reached US$2,812m, yet the airline still reported a net loss of US$257m and net margin slipping from -6.2% to -9.1%. The evidence cut both ways.

The useful takeaway is simple. When a thesis hangs on margins flipping from loss making to positive, you track the actual net margin line every quarter and test whether it is really moving toward that target level.

What JetBlue Airways' Lower Price Asks You To Believe

JetBlue Airways now trades at US$3.54, and the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St sees Fair Value above that level based on its own assumptions. That view leans on premium cabins, loyalty economics and ancillary platforms to reshape how each seat and each customer relationship earns money.

For the recent fall to look like an opportunity rather than a warning, a buyer today would need to believe JetForward execution can offset high net debt and recent losses as those premium and ancillary bets scale.

"The main thing that has to go right is successful delivery of the JetForward initiatives, including premium cabin ramp up, ancillary platforms such as Paisly, and cost and fuel recapture efforts, so that higher unit revenue and moderated non fuel unit costs can translate into sustained operating profitability and positive free cash flow targets in 2027 and 2028."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Looking One Step Beyond JetBlue

JetBlue is trying to earn more from each traveler, not just each seat. That raises a broader question about how passengers move in cities.

Short flights often compete with car rides and airport transfers. Where planes move people between regions, another platform moves them across town.

That business focuses on matching riders with drivers, couriers and freight carriers. It aims to turn everyday transportation and deliveries into a single digital habit.

If that habit deepens, the value may lie in owning the demand, not the vehicle. Your call is which side of that shift deserves more attention.

data.title: Have Vulcan Steel Insiders Been Selling Stock?
data.description:
Anyone interested in Vulcan Steel Limited (ASX:VSL) should probably be aware that the Non-Executive Chairman, Rhys Jones, recently divested AU$279k worth of shares in the company, at an average price of AU$5.58 each. However, the silver lining is that the sale only reduced their total holding by 2.2%, so we're hesitant to read anything much into it, on its own.

Trump has pledged to "unleash" American oil and gas and these 15 US stocks have developments that are poised to benefit.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Vulcan Steel

Notably, that recent sale by Non-Executive Chairman Rhys Jones was not the only time they sold Vulcan Steel shares this year. They previously made an even bigger sale of -AU$804k worth of shares at a price of AU$6.19 per share. While we don't usually like to see insider selling, it's more concerning if the sales take place at a lower price. It's of some comfort that this sale was conducted at a price well above the current share price, which is AU$5.47. So it is hard to draw any strong conclusion from it.

Over the last year, we can see that insiders have bought 43.04k shares worth AU$230k. But insiders sold 350.00k shares worth AU$2.0m. In total, Vulcan Steel insiders sold more than they bought over the last year. You can see a visual depiction of insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last 12 months, below. If you want to know exactly who sold, for how much, and when, simply click on the graph below!

Check out our latest analysis for Vulcan Steel

For those who like to find hidden gems this free list of small cap companies with recent insider purchasing, could be just the ticket.

Insider Ownership

Many investors like to check how much of a company is owned by insiders. We usually like to see fairly high levels of insider ownership. It's great to see that Vulcan Steel insiders own 34% of the company, worth about AU$272m. I like to see this level of insider ownership, because it increases the chances that management are thinking about the best interests of shareholders.

So What Does This Data Suggest About Vulcan Steel Insiders?

The insider sales have outweighed the insider buying, at Vulcan Steel, in the last three months. Despite some insider buying, the longer term picture doesn't make us feel much more positive. But it is good to see that Vulcan Steel is growing earnings. While insiders do own a lot of shares in the company (which is good), our analysis of their transactions doesn't make us feel confident about the company. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. Case in point: We've spotted 2 warning signs for Vulcan Steel you should be aware of, and 1 of them can't be ignored.

Of course, you might find a fantastic investment by looking elsewhere. So take a peek at this free list of interesting companies.

For the purposes of this article, insiders are those individuals who report their transactions to the relevant regulatory body. We currently account for open market transactions and private dispositions of direct interests only, but not derivative transactions or indirect interests.

data.title: IMAX's (NYSE:IMAX) Performance Is Even Better Than Its Earnings Suggest
data.description:
IMAX Corporation's (NYSE:IMAX) earnings announcement last week was disappointing for investors, despite the decent profit numbers. Our analysis says that investors should be optimistic, as the strong profit is built on solid foundations.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

How Do Unusual Items Influence Profit?

To properly understand IMAX's profit results, we need to consider the US$34m expense attributed to unusual items. It's never great to see unusual items costing the company profits, but on the upside, things might improve sooner rather than later. We looked at thousands of listed companies and found that unusual items are very often one-off in nature. And that's hardly a surprise given these line items are considered unusual. Assuming those unusual expenses don't come up again, we'd therefore expect IMAX to produce a higher profit next year, all else being equal.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

An Unusual Tax Situation

Just as we noted the unusual items, we must inform you that IMAX received a tax benefit which contributed US$33m to the bottom line. This is of course a bit out of the ordinary, given it is more common for companies to be paying tax than receiving tax benefits! We're sure the company was pleased with its tax benefit. However, our data indicates that tax benefits can temporarily boost statutory profit in the year it is booked, but subsequently profit may fall back. Assuming the tax benefit is not repeated every year, we could see its profitability drop noticeably, all else being equal.

Our Take On IMAX's Profit Performance

In its last report IMAX received a tax benefit which might make its profit look better than it really is on a underlying level. Having said that, it also had a unusual item reducing its profit. Given the contrasting considerations, we don't have a strong view as to whether IMAX's profits are an apt reflection of its underlying potential for profit. With this in mind, we wouldn't consider investing in a stock unless we had a thorough understanding of the risks.
